data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement GitHubPRDefenseStore backend writing defenses as PR comments (one comment per defense record). Detect head_repo != base_repo and downgrade write to no-op + log. Fork-PR review reads from TrackerDefenseStore only (read-through fallback). Cap defense_text at 4096 chars; arbiter ruling: full text in TrackerDefenseStore, summary + link in PR comment. Implement bidirectional load on local: /dso:review reads tracker by default but also reads PR comments when run against a branch with an open PR.
**Why**: SC3 PR portion. Closes the local-vs-CI defense-store split with explicit fallback for fork PRs (no GITHUB_TOKEN write scope on forks).
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - GitHubPRDefenseStore.write() / load() implemented; fork-PR detection downgrades writes to no-op
  - defense_text capped at 4096 chars; arbiter summary+link pattern enforced
  - Bidirectional load on local: tracker default, PR comments also read when PR exists for branch
  - Exponential backoff on 429 / secondary-rate-limit responses (red team #14 mitigation)
  OUT:
  - DefenseStore interface (S6)
  - Mirror workflow (S13)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, CI llm-review reads and writes defenses via GitHubPRDefenseStore for same-repo PRs and falls back to TrackerDefenseStore for fork PRs
  ← Satisfies: "DefenseStore with split backends, shared loader/writer, ticket-binding integrity, and explicit ordering contract"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Soft fallback preserves availability when GitHub API is throttled
- [Security] GITHUB_TOKEN scope on fork PRs is read-only — write attempts must fail safely

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a CI reviewer, I read and write defenses via GitHubPRDefenseStore with fork-PR fallback
